subject: Weekly Prioritization Brief — decisions requested for QBR readiness
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly Prioritization Brief — decisions requested for QBR readiness

Team —

Attaching the run-of-week prioritization brief ahead of Monday's QBR prep. This note highlights where we are on the leadership OKRs relevant to the QBR, the top 3 wins since last week, the 3 most material risks, and two specific decisions I need from the leadership distro by EOD today so engineering and sales can lock plans for the quarter close.

TL;DR
- Wins: improved 95th P99 latency on hosted API (opt path) +15%, closed two Dedicated contracts, baseline evals for v2 quantization look promising.
- Risks: model regression signal in chat evals tied to prompt-scheduling; Dedicated capacity cadence may slip if we don't approve overtime burst; pending finance approval for QBR credits could delay renewals.
- Decisions needed (choose A/B by EOD):
  1) Feature freeze for QBR packaging: Option A — soft freeze (only critical bugfixes) vs Option B — hard freeze (no commits except security). Engineering requests Option A to finish low-risk perf changes.
  2) Approve short-term burst for Dedicated nodes (2 weeks) at 30% above baseline to ensure demo reliability for two enterprise accounts (Acme, Nova). Budget estimate attached.

Details (brief)
- OKR check-ins (owner / percent to target):
  * Serving reliability (Vivek) — 72% to target; P95 within target, P99 needs tuning (engine team has a fix queued).
  * Cost per token (Monica) — 60% to target; Optimize suggestions applied but rollout delayed pending freeze decision.
  * New enterprise commitments (Laura) — 85% to target; two deals in signature stage (Acme, Nova).

- Wins (since last update):
  1) P99 perf improvement: +15% on hosted for default sequence by runtime kernel swap (perf bench attached).
  2) Sales: closed Dedicated renewal with Nova — favorable net retention impact.
  3) Evals: v2 quantized model baseline shows matched perplexity in 90% of prompt sets (internal evals linked).

- Risks / Blockers:
  1) Prompt-scheduling regression: production traffic shows a 2% drop in relevance for chat flows after a recent prompt rewriter change. Root cause suspected in ordering heuristics. (Mitigation: rollback or canary on 3% traffic).
  2) Dedicated pool scaling: node provisioning lead times are 5–7 days; without burst approval some demos will run on soft-fallback models.
  3) Finance: approval for QBR credits (customer-facing credits to close renewals) pending — finance requested an exec sign-off for amounts >$50k.

Next steps / asks
- Please reply with your choices for Decision 1 (freeze A or B) and Decision 2 (approve burst: yes/no) by EOD PST.
- If you want a short sync, propose 30-minute window between 11:00–14:00 PT.

Attachments: QBR-priority-matrix.xlsx, feature-freeze-proposal.md

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly Prioritization Brief — decisions requested for QBR readiness

Rishi —

Acknowledged and thanks for the concise brief. Quick answers from my side:
- Decision 1 (feature freeze): I lean toward Option A (soft freeze). We need the low-risk perf changes to hit the P99 goals — if engineering can gate changes via canary or flag, I'm supportive.
- Decision 2 (burst approval): Tentatively yes for the 2-week burst for Acme and Nova demos, contingent on finance sign-off. Please include the expected cost delta in the doc for an exec sign-off.

Two asks for the runbook:
1) Add a short mitigation play for the prompt-scheduling regression (rollback timeline + owner).
2) Add staging checklist for Dedicated demo configurations so sales can validate before customer-facing sessions.

If helpful I can hop on a quick call at 11:30 PT.

Laura
Laura Bennett
SVP, Sales & GTM, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
